    ----------
    memory : :class:`Memory`
        Memory associated with the port.
    domain : str
        Clock domain. Defaults to ``"sync"``. Writes have a latency of 1 clock cycle.
    granularity : int
        Port granularity. Defaults to ``memory.width``. Write data is split evenly in
        ``memory.width // granularity`` chunks, which can be updated independently.

    ----------
    memory : :class:`Memory`
    domain : str
    granularity : int
    addr : Signal(range(memory.depth)), in

    data : Signal(memory.width), in

                             "({} > {})"

        self.domain       = domain
        self.granularity  = granularity

                           name=f"{memory.name}_w_data", src_loc_at=1 + src_loc_at)

    Parameters
    ----------
    shape : int
        Width of each memory element in bits.
    depth : int
        Number of memory elements.
    init : list of int

class MemoryRow:
    """A row of memory data.

    This class represents a single row of memory data and is used for simulation purposes.
    """

    def __init__(self, data, index):
        self._data = data
        self._index = index

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"(memory-row {self._data!r} {self._index})"

    def __eq__(self, other):
        # This is needed for the test to pass
        if not isinstance(other, MemoryRow):
            return False
        return self._data is other._data and self._index == other._index

334:     def collect_init_attrs(self):
335:         # Flip-flops are special in Yosys; the initial value is stored not as a cell parameter but
336:         # as an attribute of a wire connected to the output of the flip-flop. The claimed benefit
337:         # of this arrangement is that fine cells, which cannot have parameters (so that certain
338:         # backends, like BLIF, which cannot represent parameters--or attributes--can be used to
339:         # emit these cells), then do not need to have 3x more variants (one for initialized to 0,
340:         # one for 1, one for X).
341:         #
342:         # At the time of writing, 2024-02-11, Yosys has 125 (one hundred twenty five) fine FF cells,
343:         # which are generated by a Python script because they have gotten completely out of hand
344:         # long ago and no one could keep track of them manually. This list features such beauties
345:         # as $_DFFSRE_PPPN_ and its other 7 cousins.
346:         #
347:         # These are real cells, used by real Yosys developers! Look at what they have done for us,
348:         # with all the subtly unsynthesizable Verilog we sent them and all of the incompatibilities
349:         # with vendor toolchains we reported!
350:         #
351:         # Nothing is fine about these cells. The decision to have `init` as a wire attribute is
352:         # quite possibly the single worst design decision in Yosys, and not having to dealing with
353:         # that bullshit again is enough of a reason to implement an FPGA toolchain from scratch.
354:         #
355:         # Just have 375 fine cells, bro. Trust me bro. You will certainly not regret having 375
356:         # fine cells in your toolchain. Or at least you will be able to process netlists without
357:         # having to special-case this one godforsaken attribute every time you look at a wire.
358:         #
359:         # -- @whitequark
360:         for cell_idx in self.module.cells:
361:             cell = self.netlist.cells[cell_idx]
362:             if isinstance(cell, _nir.FlipFlop):
363:                 width = len(cell.data)
364:                 attrs = {"init": _ast.Const(cell.init, width), **cell.attributes}
365:                 value = _nir.Value(_nir.Net.from_cell(cell_idx, bit) for bit in range(width))
366:                 self.value_attrs[value] = attrs

368:     def emit_signal_wires(self):
369:         for signal, name in self.module.signal_names.items():
370:             value = self.netlist.signals[signal]
371: 
372:             # One of: (1) empty and created here, (2) `init` filled in by `collect_init_attrs`,
373:             # (3) populated by some other signal aliasing the same nets. In the last case, we will
374:             # glue attributes for these signals together, but synthesizers (including Yosys, when
375:             # the design is flattened) will do that anyway, so it doesn't matter.
376:             attrs = self.value_attrs.setdefault(value, {})
377:             attrs.update(signal.attrs)
378:             self.value_src_loc[value] = signal.src_loc
379: 
380:             for repr in signal._value_repr:
381:                 if repr.path == () and isinstance(repr.format, _repr.FormatEnum):
382:                     enum = repr.format.enum
383:                     attrs["enum_base_type"] = enum.__name__
384:                     for enum_value in enum:
385:                         attrs["enum_value_{:0{}b}".format(enum_value.value, signal.width)] = enum_value.name
386: 
387:             if name in self.module.ports:
388:                 port_value, _flow = self.module.ports[name]
389:                 assert value == port_value
390:                 self.name_map[signal] = (*self.module.name, name)
391:             else:
392:                 wire = self.builder.wire(width=signal.width, signed=signal.signed,
393:                                          name=name, attrs=attrs,
394:                                          src=_src(signal.src_loc))
395:                 self.sigport_wires[name] = (wire, value)
396:                 self.name_map[signal] = (*self.module.name, wire[1:])

398:     def emit_port_wires(self):
399:         named_signals = {name: signal for signal, name in self.module.signal_names.items()}
400:         for port_id, (name, (value, flow)) in enumerate(self.module.ports.items()):
401:             signed = False
402:             if name in named_signals:
403:                 signed = named_signals[name].signed
404:             wire = self.builder.wire(width=len(value), signed=signed,
405:                                      port_id=port_id, port_kind=flow.value,
406:                                      name=name, attrs=self.value_attrs.get(value, {}),
407:                                      src=_src(self.value_src_loc.get(value)))
408:             self.sigport_wires[name] = (wire, value)
409:             if flow == _nir.ModuleNetFlow.Output:
410:                 continue
411:             # If we just emitted an input port, it is driving the value.
412:             self.driven_sigports.add(name)
413:             for bit, net in enumerate(value):

433:     def emit_driven_wire(self, value):
434:         # Emits a wire for a value, in preparation for driving it.
435:         if value in self.value_names:
436:             # If there is a signal or port matching this value, reuse its wire as the canonical
437:             # wire of the nets involved.
438:             name = self.value_names[value]
439:             wire, named_value = self.sigport_wires[name]
440:             assert value == named_value, \
441:                 f"Inconsistent values {value!r}, {named_value!r} for wire {name!r}"

444:             # Otherwise, make an anonymous wire.

447:             self.nets[net] = (wire, bit)

493:     def sigspec(self, *parts: '_nir.Net | Iterable[_nir.Net]'):
494:         value = _nir.Value()
495:         for part in parts:
496:             value += _nir.Value(part)
497: 
498:         chunks = []
499:         begin_pos = 0
500:         while begin_pos < len(value):
501:             end_pos = begin_pos
502:             if value[begin_pos].is_const:
503:                 while end_pos < len(value) and value[end_pos].is_const:
504:                     end_pos += 1
505:                 width = end_pos - begin_pos
506:                 bits = "".join(str(net.const) for net in value[begin_pos:end_pos])
507:                 chunks.append(f"{width}'{bits[::-1]}")
508:             else:
509:                 wire, start_bit = self.nets[value[begin_pos]]
510:                 bit = start_bit
511:                 while (end_pos < len(value) and
512:                         not value[end_pos].is_const and
513:                         self.nets[value[end_pos]] == (wire, bit)):
514:                     end_pos += 1
515:                     bit += 1
516:                 width = end_pos - begin_pos
517:                 if width == 1:
518:                     chunks.append(f"{wire} [{start_bit}]")
519:                 else:
520:                     chunks.append(f"{wire} [{start_bit + width - 1}:{start_bit}]")
521:             begin_pos = end_pos
522: 
523:         if len(chunks) == 1:
524:             return chunks[0]
525:         return "{ " + " ".join(reversed(chunks)) + " }"

567:     def emit_assignment_list(self, cell_idx, cell):
568:         def emit_assignments(case, cond):
569:             # Emits assignments from the assignment list into the given case.
570:             # ``cond`` is the net which is the condition for ``case`` being active.
571:             # Returns once it hits an assignment whose condition is not nested within ``cond``,
572:             # letting parent invocation take care of the remaining assignments.
573:             nonlocal pos
574: 
575:             emitted_switch = False
576:             while pos < len(cell.assignments):
577:                 assign = cell.assignments[pos]
578:                 if assign.cond == cond and not emitted_switch:
579:                     # Not nested, and we didn't emit a switch yet, so emit the assignment.
580:                     case.assign(self.sigspec(lhs[assign.start:assign.start + len(assign.value)]),
581:                                 self.sigspec(assign.value))
582:                     pos += 1
583:                 elif assign.cond == cond:
584:                     # Not nested, but we emitted a subswitch. Wrap the assignments in a dummy
585:                     # switch. This is necessary because Yosys executes all assignments before all
586:                     # subswitches (but allows you to mix asssignments and switches in RTLIL, for
587:                     # maximum confusion).
588:                     with case.switch("{ }") as switch:
589:                         with switch.case("") as subcase:
590:                             while pos < len(cell.assignments):
591:                                 assign = cell.assignments[pos]
592:                                 if assign.cond == cond:
593:                                     subcase.assign(self.sigspec(lhs[assign.start:assign.start +
594:                                                                     len(assign.value)]),
595:                                                    self.sigspec(assign.value))
596:                                     pos += 1
597:                                 else:
598:                                     break
599:                 else:
600:                     # Condition doesn't match this case's condition — either we encountered
601:                     # a nested condition, or we should break out.  Try to find out exactly
602:                     # how we are nested.
603:                     search_cond = assign.cond
604:                     while True:
605:                         if search_cond == cond:
606:                             # We have found the PriorityMatch cell that we should enter.
607:                             break
608:                         if search_cond == _nir.Net.from_const(1):
609:                             # If this isn't nested condition, go back to parent invocation.
610:                             return
611:                         # Grab the PriorityMatch cell that is on the next level of nesting.
612:                         priority_cell_idx = search_cond.cell
613:                         priority_cell = self.netlist.cells[priority_cell_idx]
614:                         assert isinstance(priority_cell, _nir.PriorityMatch)
615:                         search_cond = priority_cell.en
616:                     # We assume that:
617:                     # 1. PriorityMatch inputs can only be Match cell outputs, or constant 1.
618:                     # 2. All Match cells driving a given PriorityMatch cell test the same value.
619:                     # Grab the tested value from a random Match cell.
620:                     test = _nir.Value()
621:                     for net in priority_cell.inputs:
622:                         if net != _nir.Net.from_const(1):
623:                             matches_cell = self.netlist.cells[net.cell]
624:                             assert isinstance(matches_cell, _nir.Matches)
625:                             test = matches_cell.value
626:                             break
627:                     # Now emit cases for all PriorityMatch inputs, in sequence. Consume as many
628:                     # assignments as possible along the way.
629:                     with case.switch(self.sigspec(test)) as switch:
630:                         for bit, net in enumerate(priority_cell.inputs):
631:                             subcond = _nir.Net.from_cell(priority_cell_idx, bit)
632:                             if net == _nir.Net.from_const(1):
633:                                 patterns = ()
634:                             else:
635:                                 # Validate the above assumptions.
636:                                 matches_cell = self.netlist.cells[net.cell]
637:                                 assert isinstance(matches_cell, _nir.Matches)
638:                                 assert test == matches_cell.value
639:                                 patterns = matches_cell.patterns
640:                             with switch.case(*patterns) as subcase:
641:                                 emit_assignments(subcase, subcond)
642:                     emitted_switch = True
643: 
644:         lhs = _nir.Value(_nir.Net.from_cell(cell_idx, bit) for bit in range(len(cell.default)))
645:         with self.builder.process(src=_src(cell.src_loc)) as proc:
646:             with proc.case() as root_case:
647:                 root_case.assign(self.sigspec(lhs), self.sigspec(cell.default))
648: 
649:                 pos = 0 # nonlocally used in `emit_assignments`
650:                 emit_assignments(root_case, _nir.Net.from_const(1))
651:                 assert pos == len(cell.assignments)
